summary: Charles Gabriel Seligman was an Indology scholar who studied at St Thomas' Hospital (~1892–1896). He held a post at the University of London (~1910–1934) and taught Bronislaw Malinowski.

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Charles Goodman earned his PhD from the University of Michigan in 2002 under Allan Gibbard. He served as an Associate Professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

Charles H. Long, a religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Chicago (~1948–1962). He held posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1974–1990), Syracuse University (~1987–1990), Chicago (1993), and UC Santa Barbara (2005).

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Charles Hallisey studied at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1980–1988). He held appointments at Loyola Chicago, Amherst College, UW–Madison (~2001–2007), and Harvard University (~1991–2000, ~2007).

Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1854–1858), where he was later Fellow and Tutor (1860). He served as Chair of History and Principal at Presidency University, Kolkata (1866–1892), and Librarian at the India Office (1892–1903).

Charles Malamoud studied at the University of Paris (~1948–1960) and worked in Indology and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Lyon (~1968–1979) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études as Directeur d'Études (~1979–1999).

An Indology and linguistics scholar, Charles Philip Brown studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College (~1814–1817). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1855) and as Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1865–1879).

Charles Ramble works in Tibetology and religious studies, having studied at Durham University and under Michael Aris. He held posts at Tribhuvan University, Wolfson College, Oxford (~2000–2009), the University of Oxford (attested 2006–2015), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2009).

Charles Rieu studied at Geneva and Bonn under Jean Humbert, G. W. Freytag, Johannes Gildemeister, and Christian Lassen. Working in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he served at the British Museum (from 1847) and as Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

An Indologist and linguist, Charles Rockwell Lanman studied at Yale and under William Dwight Whitney and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Johns Hopkins (~1876–1880) and Harvard University (from 1880), where he founded the Harvard Oriental Series.

A Buddhist and religious studies scholar, Charles S. Prebish studied at Case Western Reserve, under David M. Miller, and under Richard Hugh Robinson. He held positions at Penn State (~1972–2007), the University of Calgary (~2007), and Utah State University (attested 2017).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1956) and the University of Illinois (~1965–1969), working in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Ohio University (~1969–1972).

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist who co-founded the Asiatic Society (~1784–1836). He held long-term posts with the East India Company (~1770–1836) and served as Librarian for the India Office Library and Records (~1801–1836).

Charles de Harlez was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a Professor, including as Professor of Oriental Languages, at KU Leuven (~1871–1899) and taught Louis de La Vallée Poussin.

Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sera Khandro (~1931–1940) and Dorje Dradul, and his students included Keith Dowman and Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh, active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities. She served as Professor of Philosophy at Thammasat University (~1973–2000) and founded the Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women.

Chen-kuo Lin is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral studies at Temple University in 1991. He held professorships at National Chengchi University (attested 1997–1999, 2014–2018) and positions at Leiden University and IIAS.
Cheng Yen is a religious and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Yin Shun (~1963–2005) and founded Tzu Chi.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a scholar in the field of Japanology who studied under William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.
Chi Chen Ho is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Hsuan Hua and earned a PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., also serving there as a Teaching Assistant.
